title: Long-term Observations of Patients with Macular Telangiectasia Type 2 (MEMORY Study)
summary: Macular Telangiectasia Type 2 (MacTel 2) is a rare disease of the central retina (macula), with a prevalence of about 1 in 3,000, which can lead to chronic and irreversible vision deterioration, potentially resulting in blindness. The disease typically begins in individuals over the age of 40 and progresses chronically in both eyes. The causes of the disease remain unclear, and there is currently no approved treatment. Existing scientific findings suggest that MacTel 2 is a neurodegenerative disorder, where a loss of function in the central retinal support cells leads to thinning of the retina and subsequent changes in the retinal blood vessels. Promising therapeutic outcomes with intraocular application of neuroprotective substances (Ciliary Neurotrophic Factor, CNTF) are currently being reported in clinical trials. Approval of this treatment approach is currently under review by the relevant authorities in the USA. A key prerequisite for effective treatment indication will be identifying suitable MacTel 2 patients who exhibit rapid disease progression and would therefore benefit from early therapy. However, little is known about the long-term disease progression of MacTel 2. Therefore, in order to make informed treatment decisions in the future, fundamental data on the spontaneous long-term course of the disease, as well as the identification of prognostic factors for either slow or rapid vision loss, are essential.
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Clinical diagnosis of MacTel 2
Written consent form
Exclusion criteria:
Refusal or lack of consent to pseudonymized documentation and electronic storage of personal data
